transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help you with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have some questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: According to the information I have, you can start doing light exercise, such as gardening, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid strenuous or heavy exercise, lifting heavy objects, or activities that might get water in your eye, especially in the first month after surgery. So, just take it easy and start with some light gardening when you feel ready.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That makes sense, thank you! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use the eye drops as prescribed. If you're running out, you can get some more from your GP. And if you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma or dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. So, you can start using your eye drops as usual.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, thanks for clearing that up. I'm also wondering, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal to be a bit sensitive to light after cataract surgery, especially when it's bright. Mild sensitivity is okay, and you can just wear sunglasses when you're going outside. But if the pain is significant or severe, and your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess it further.
